meta.title: English Future Perfect Continuous Tenses Test
meta.description: A comprehensive test covering English Future Perfect Continuous Tenses themed around family, combining at least one or more grammar topics per question.
meta.info: This test includes 30 questions focusing on combined grammar structures involving the Future Perfect Continuous tense paired with topics like conditionals, relative clauses, gerunds, inversion, and more, all within familiar family contexts.
meta.author: Qwen3.7

data.hint: Choose the correct verb form to complete the sentence.
data.question: By the time the baby turns one, we _____ in this house for a decade.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Perfect Continuous tense with a time clause. 'Will have been living' emphasizes the duration of an action up to a specific future point.
explanation.concept: Using Future Perfect Continuous for actions in progress up to a future time
explanation.formula: By the time + present simple, subject + will have been + verb-ing
examples: By next year, I will have been working here for a decade.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Perfect Continuous tense with a non-defining relative clause. 'Will have been' must be followed by the present participle 'celebrating'.
explanation.concept: Forming the Future Perfect Continuous within relative clauses
explanation.formula: Noun, who + will have been + verb-ing, + present continuous verb
examples: My parents, who will have been married for 30 years, are celebrating.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb form to complete the sentence.
data.question: I look forward to seeing my cousins, as we _____ each other for years by the time of the reunion.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Perfect Continuous tense with gerund verb patterns. 'Will have been missing' emphasizes the ongoing duration of the feeling up to the future event.
explanation.concept: Future Perfect Continuous following prepositional phrases requiring gerunds
explanation.formula: Look forward to + verb-ing, as + subject + will have been + verb-ing
examples: I look forward to seeing them, as we will have been waiting for months.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Perfect Continuous tense with quantifiers and subject-verb agreement. 'A number of' takes a plural verb, while 'the number of' takes a singular verb ('has been').
explanation.topic: Future Perfect Continuous + Quantifiers + Subject-Verb Agreement
explanation.concept: Agreement with 'a number of' vs. 'the number of'
explanation.formula: A number of + plural noun + will have been + verb-ing; the number of + singular verb
examples: A number of cars have arrived, but the number of spots has decreased.

data.question: If the flight is delayed, we _____ at the airport for over six hours by midnight.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Perfect Continuous tense with a First Conditional structure. The Future Continuous aspect emphasizes the duration of the waiting up to the future time marker.
explanation.concept: Using Future Perfect Continuous in the main clause of a first conditional
explanation.formula: If + present simple, subject + will have been + verb-ing + by + future time
examples: If it rains, we will have been waiting for hours.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Perfect Continuous tense with preposition collocations. The verb 'rely' is always followed by the preposition 'on', not 'in'.
explanation.concept: Correct preposition usage after specific verbs in continuous tenses
explanation.formula: Subject + will have been + relying on + noun
examples: He will have been relying on his savings for months.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb form to complete the sentence.
data.question: The family business has been struggling; therefore, by next month, my father _____ overtime for a full year.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Perfect Continuous tense with discourse markers. 'Therefore' links the ongoing struggle to the future completed duration of working overtime.
explanation.concept: Using resultative discourse markers with Future Perfect Continuous contexts
explanation.formula: Present perfect continuous clause; therefore, + subject + will have been + verb-ing
examples: Sales are down; therefore, we will have been cutting costs for a year.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Perfect Continuous tense with negative adverbial inversion. 'Rarely' at the beginning triggers subject-auxiliary inversion ('Rarely will the children'), and 'have been' requires the present participle 'behaving'.
explanation.concept: Subject-auxiliary inversion with negative adverbs in Future Perfect Continuous
explanation.formula: Rarely + will + subject + have been + verb-ing
examples: Never will the team have been playing this well.

data.question: It is my mother who _____ the household finances for the longest time by the time she retires.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Perfect Continuous tense with a cleft sentence for emphasis. 'Will have been managing' highlights the duration of the action up to a future point.
explanation.concept: Using Future Perfect Continuous in it-cleft structures
explanation.formula: It is + noun + who + will have been + verb-ing + by the time + present simple
examples: It is the teacher who will have been preparing the lessons for weeks.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Perfect Continuous tense with modal verbs of deduction. Modal verbs ('must') are always followed by the base form 'have', and the continuous aspect requires the present participle 'driving'.
explanation.concept: Modal perfect continuous constructions
explanation.formula: Subject + must + have been + verb-ing
examples: He must have been working all night.

data.question: As the family grows, the parents _____ their parenting styles continuously to meet new challenges.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Perfect Continuous tense with conjunctions of time. 'Will have been adapting' emphasizes the ongoing, changing nature of the action leading up to a future point.
explanation.concept: Describing changing situations with 'as' using Future Perfect Continuous
explanation.formula: As + subject + verb + s/es, subject + will have been + verb-ing
examples: As the child grows, the parents will have been adapting their methods.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Perfect Continuous tense with ellipsis. To maintain the parallel Future Perfect Continuous structure, 'not have' must be followed by 'been renovating', not just 'renovating'.
explanation.concept: Maintaining parallel Future Perfect Continuous structure in compound sentences
explanation.formula: Subject + will have been + verb-ing, but + subject + will not have + been + verb-ing
examples: I will have been studying, but she will not have been studying.

data.question: The more the toddler cries, the more exhausted the parents _____ by the end of the week.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Perfect Continuous tense with advanced comparative structures. 'Will have been feeling' emphasizes the accumulating duration of exhaustion.
explanation.concept: Using Future Perfect Continuous in double comparative structures
explanation.formula: The more + subject + verb + s/es, the more + adjective + subject + will have been + verb-ing
examples: The harder it rains, the more flooded the streets will have been getting.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Perfect Continuous tense with phrasal verbs. 'Will have been' must be followed by the present participle 'catching' to form the continuous aspect of the phrasal verb 'catch up'.
explanation.concept: Forming the continuous aspect of separable and inseparable phrasal verbs
explanation.formula: Subject + will have been + verb-ing + particle
examples: They will have been catching up for hours.

data.question: We _____ a unique family tradition for twenty years by next Christmas, making it a truly special milestone.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Perfect Continuous tense with article usage. 'Unique' starts with a consonant sound (/j/), so it correctly takes the indefinite article 'a', and 'will have been celebrating' marks the duration.
explanation.concept: Indefinite articles before words starting with a /j/ sound in Future Perfect Continuous contexts
explanation.formula: Subject + will have been + verb-ing + a + word starting with /j/ sound
examples: They will have been building a unique legacy.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Perfect Continuous tense with 'not only... but also' inversion. 'Will have been' must be followed by the present participle 'funding' to maintain the continuous aspect.
explanation.topic: Future Perfect Continuous + Not Only ... But Also
explanation.concept: Subject-auxiliary inversion with 'not only' in Future Perfect Continuous
explanation.formula: Not only + will + subject + have been + verb-ing, but + subject + will + also + have been + verb-ing
examples: Not only will she have been teaching, but she will also have been mentoring.

data.question: Under no circumstances _____ such disrespectful behavior from the teenagers, especially after all the sacrifices we have made.

A.text: will the parents have been tolerating

B.text: the parents will have been tolerating

explanation.text: This combines the Future Perfect Continuous tense with negative adverbial inversion. 'Under no circumstances' at the beginning triggers subject-auxiliary inversion ('will the parents have been tolerating').
explanation.topic: Future Perfect Continuous + Negative Adverbial Inversion
explanation.concept: Subject-auxiliary inversion with negative phrases in Future Perfect Continuous
explanation.formula: Under no circumstances + will + subject + have been + verb-ing
examples: Under no circumstances will we have been accepting this.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Perfect Continuous tense with conditional inversion. 'Will have been' must be followed by the present participle 'babysitting' to form the continuous aspect.
explanation.concept: Forming the continuous aspect after inverted conditional clauses
explanation.formula: Should + subject + base verb, subject + will have been + verb-ing
examples: Should you need help, I will have been preparing for this.

data.question: Were I to move back to my hometown, I realize I _____ my extended family for too long by the time I actually visit.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Perfect Continuous tense with second conditional inversion. 'Will have been missing' emphasizes the accumulating duration of the feeling up to the hypothetical future visit.
explanation.concept: Future Perfect Continuous in the main clause of an inverted second conditional
explanation.formula: Were + subject + to + base verb, subject + will have been + verb-ing
examples: Were I to leave, I will have been regretting it.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Perfect Continuous tense with mixed conditionals. The plural subject 'we' requires the plural auxiliary 'will have', not 'will has'.
explanation.concept: Subject-verb agreement in Future Perfect Continuous within mixed conditional structures
explanation.formula: If + past perfect, subject + would + base verb, even though + subject + will have + been + verb-ing
examples: If I had studied, I would be smarter, even though I will have been trying.

data.question: It is high time we acknowledged that the babysitter _____ for us for five years by next month.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Perfect Continuous tense with the 'it's high time' structure. 'Will have been working' correctly marks the duration of the action up to the future point.
explanation.topic: Future Perfect Continuous + It's High Time
explanation.concept: Using Future Perfect Continuous in noun clauses following 'it's high time'
explanation.formula: It is high time + subject + past simple + that + subject + will have been + verb-ing
examples: It is high time we recognized that he will have been leading for a decade.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Perfect Continuous tense with 'as though' unreal comparisons. 'Acts' is the correct third-person singular present simple, and 'will have been' requires the present participle 'running'.
explanation.topic: Future Perfect Continuous + As Though / As If
explanation.concept: Forming the continuous aspect in unreal comparisons
explanation.formula: Subject + acts + as though + subject + will have been + verb-ing
examples: He acts as though he will have been knowing the answer.

explanation.topic: Future Perfect Continuous + So / Such Inversion
explanation.concept: Subject-auxiliary inversion with 'so' in Future Perfect Continuous contexts
explanation.formula: So + adjective + will + subject + be + that + subject + will have been + verb-ing
examples: So difficult will it be that we will have been struggling for months.

explanation.concept: Subject-verb agreement in Future Perfect Continuous within noun clauses
explanation.formula: What + present simple + is that + plural subject + will have + been + verb-ing

data.question: I intend to visit my relatives soon, as I _____ our family bond for too long, and I feel guilty about it.

explanation.concept: Using Future Perfect Continuous to express duration following intention verbs
explanation.formula: Subject + intend + to-infinitive, as + subject + will have been + verb-ing
examples: I intend to call him, as I will have been ignoring his messages.

explanation.topic: Future Perfect Continuous + Prepositions after Adjectives
explanation.concept: Correct preposition usage after specific adjectives in Future Perfect Continuous contexts
explanation.formula: Subject + will have been + accustomed to + verb-ing

data.question: Few of the extended family members _____ the annual gatherings, while little of the family heirloom has been preserved.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Perfect Continuous tense with quantifiers. 'Few of' is used with countable plural nouns ('members'), and 'will have been attending' emphasizes the duration up to a future point.
explanation.concept: Countable quantifiers with Future Perfect Continuous subjects
explanation.formula: Few of + plural countable noun + will have been + verb-ing
examples: Few of the students will have been studying.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Perfect Continuous tense with perfect participle clauses. 'Having been' requires the present participle 'raising', and the passive Future Perfect Continuous requires the past participle 'exhausted'.
explanation.concept: Perfect participle clauses paired with Future Perfect Continuous passive
explanation.formula: Having been + verb-ing, subject + will have been + past participle
examples: Having been working all day, he will have been exhausted.

data.question: The family insists that the estate _____ properly by the time it is handed down to the next generation.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Perfect Passive tense with the mandative subjunctive. 'Insists that' can be followed by a future perfect passive construction to emphasize completion before a future event.
explanation.concept: Future Perfect Passive in noun clauses following verbs of insistence
explanation.formula: Subject + insists + that + subject + will have been + past participle
examples: They insist that the project will have been completed by Friday.

explanation.formula: Subject + will have been + adverb + verb-ing
